tagline: Free QR codes made right in your browser (manageqrcodes.com) — sign in with Luckee only if you want to save them to My codes.
summary: Manage QR Codes generates styled QR codes entirely in the browser with `qr-code-styling`: pick a type (URL, Wi-Fi, vCard, email, SMS, phone, text, location, event, WhatsApp, PayPal, Zoom), fill in the fields, style it and download PNG/SVG or PDF. No server call is needed to create or download a code.

A Luckee account is optional. After your first code a modal offers to save it; signed-in users get **My codes**, a list they can reopen and edit, stored through a small hosted CMS API backed by Supabase. A separate open-source Express server offers `POST /api/generate-code` (URL → PNG) for integrators; the web app doesn't use it.
audience: Anyone who needs a quick QR code without signing up.
Small businesses who want to keep and re-edit their codes (menus, Wi-Fi, contact cards).
Developers who want a tiny self-hosted URL → PNG QR endpoint.
notFor: Dynamic / trackable QR codes with scan analytics — codes encode content directly.
Bulk generation in the web app — one code at a time (integrators can script the OSS API).
Gating — generating and downloading never require an account.

capabilities.title: In-browser generator
capabilities.detail: The landing page's `#generator` section: 12 QR types, design controls and live preview, all client-side.

capabilities.title: Optional save
capabilities.detail: A one-time modal after your first code ("Continue without saving" available) signs you up or in and saves the code.

capabilities.title: My codes
capabilities.detail: `/codes` and `/code-detail-page` (signed-in only) list and edit saved codes via `/api/qr-codes`.

capabilities.title: OSS QR API
capabilities.detail: `POST /api/generate-code` with `{ url }` returns a PNG; `/docs` and `/api-docs.json` document it.

components.name: Web app
components.stack: Next.js, Redux Toolkit, `qr-code-styling`, `jspdf`, Supabase JS, Vercel Analytics
components.owns: Landing + generator, Luckee sign-in/sign-up, My codes, `/learn`. Calls the CMS at `NEXT_PUBLIC_CMS_URL` with the Supabase JWT.

components.name: Save API (CMS)
components.owns: Saved QR codes CRUD and account sync for signed-in users (`supabase/migrations/`).

components.name: OSS QR API
components.owns: `POST /api/generate-code` (URL → PNG), docs page and API catalog. Stateless.

dataFlow: The browser builds the QR payload for the chosen type and renders it with `qr-code-styling`; downloads happen locally.
If you choose to save, the browser signs in with Luckee Supabase and calls the CMS (`NEXT_PUBLIC_CMS_URL`) with the JWT.
The CMS verifies the JWT, syncs the account and stores the code in Supabase.
Separately, integrators call the OSS server's `POST /api/generate-code` to get a PNG.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: Everything you type into a code stays in the browser unless you save it.

trust.title: CMS
trust.detail: Supabase service role key; trusts only valid Luckee JWTs.

commonTasks.title: Run the web app locally
commonTasks.when: Working on the generator or landing.
steps: Clone `qr-code-generator-web` (Hub has no web path for this project yet — see Hub notes).
`npm run dev`; the generator works even without the CMS.

commonTasks.title: Run the save API
steps: Apply `supabase/migrations/` to the Luckee Supabase project.
Set `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in the CMS `.env` (port 3042) and start it.

commonTasks.title: Generate a PNG from a script

troubleshooting.fix: The CMS isn't reachable at `NEXT_PUBLIC_CMS_URL` or its Supabase env is wrong.

troubleshooting.symptom: Sign-up says check your email but nothing arrives
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm Supabase email settings and that the site URL is in the redirect list.

troubleshooting.symptom: Scanned code opens the wrong thing
troubleshooting.fix: Check the type-specific fields (e.g. Wi-Fi security type, vCard fields) in the preview before downloading.
hub.local.json points at the OSS server, not the CMS the web app uses.

glossary.definition: The hosted save API for My codes (qr-code-generator-express-server-cms).
The standalone URL → PNG server for integrators.
Saved codes for signed-in Luckee users.

hubNotes: hub.local.json has no `webDir` for this project and its `expressDir` points at `qr-code-generator-open-source-express-server`, while the registry lists `qr-code-generator-express-server-cms` + `qr-code-generator-web`. All three are cloned in `~/github/qr-code-generator/`.
With no `webPortStart`, the web would fall back to the registry's 3041, which website-site-scraper also uses.
The CMS README is still the template; its `.env.example` (port 3042, Supabase) is accurate.
